change: Recognised modern-slavery victims on Skilled Worker visas can leave abusive sponsors and work for any employer for the remainder of their visa
affected_cohort: Skilled Worker visa holders formally recognised by the Home Office as modern-slavery victims
observed_fact: Home Office states recognised victims are no longer tied to the specific sponsor and may take any lawful work for the remainder of existing permission.
pathway_mechanism: Reduces sponsor lock-in and downside risk for a narrow, vulnerable cohort; may improve ability to switch jobs after recognition.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially lowers effective labour-access/friction energy for this cohort; no numeric score applied.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Not a general relaxation of Skilled Worker switching rules; do not extrapolate to all sponsored workers or all migrant profiles.

change: ONE Pass (AI and Tech) track announced; intended to replace Tech.Pass from January 2027
affected_cohort: Highly paid AI/technology leaders and senior technical talent meeting company and experience criteria
observed_fact: MOM says the track will accept a combination of cash and assessed vested non-cash compensation for the salary criterion; published criteria include high compensation and at least five years of relevant experience.
pathway_mechanism: May increase flexibility for a narrow high-end talent segment while leaving most ordinary work-pass applicants outside this route.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially lowers access friction for eligible top AI/tech talent; no broad destination energy change assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Eligibility is highly selective; future rules and implementation details can change. This is not a general work-visa liberalisation.

change: Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salary thresholds scheduled to increase for new applications
affected_cohort: New Employment Pass and S Pass applications from January 2027; renewals for passes expiring from January 2028
observed_fact: MOM announced minimum EP salary increasing from SGD 5,600 to 6,000 (financial services 6,200 to 6,600) and S Pass from SGD 3,300 to 3,600 (financial services 3,800 to 4,000), with age-graded thresholds.
pathway_mechanism: Raises the salary hurdle for some employer-sponsored applicants while maintaining higher salary norms and targeting workforce composition.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially increases entry friction for candidates near the old thresholds; may be neutral for applicants well above thresholds. No numeric score assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Future effective date; do not apply these thresholds to applications before the stated dates or treat them as observed migration outcomes.
observation_period: New applications from 2027-01-01; affected renewals from 2028-01-01

change: Minimum annual remuneration thresholds increased for employment permits
affected_cohort: New employment permit applicants in relevant permit categories, subject to category-specific rules and phased changes
observed_fact: Government roadmap raised the General Employment Permit minimum from EUR 34,000 to EUR 36,605 and Critical Skills Employment Permit minimum from EUR 38,000 to EUR 40,904 from 1 March 2026.
pathway_mechanism: Raises the wage/eligibility hurdle for jobs below the new thresholds; may also reduce undercutting and align thresholds with wage growth.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially raises access-friction energy for lower-paid eligible applicants; no numeric score assigned.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Thresholds are permit-specific and have further phased changes through 2030; eligibility and exemptions must be modelled by route and occupation.
publisher: Ireland Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment

change: 2026 Express Entry category-based selection priorities published
status: Current selection framework; invitations depend on rounds and eligibility
affected_cohort: Eligible Express Entry candidates in category-based rounds
observed_fact: IRCC added categories including doctors, researchers and senior managers with Canadian work experience, transport occupations, and skilled military recruits with a job offer; renewed categories include French, health/social services, education, STEM and trades.
pathway_mechanism: Changes the relative invitation opportunities for candidates who meet targeted category criteria; it does not guarantee invitation or permanent residence.
directional_eom_impact: Potentially improves relative pathway attractiveness for eligible profiles; not a uniform positive shift for all applicants.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Category-based selection supplements other rounds; actual selection depends on CRS scores, category eligibility and invitation rounds. No numeric score assigned.

change: Opposition proposal to reduce temporary visa numbers and alter student/graduate pathways reported
status: Opposition proposal; not enacted government policy
affected_cohort: Potentially temporary visa holders, international students and temporary graduates if adopted
observed_fact: Reuters reported an opposition proposal for substantial temporary-visa reductions and changes to student and graduate routes.
pathway_mechanism: Could affect expected route availability if enacted, but currently represents political uncertainty rather than a rule in force.
directional_eom_impact: Watchlist risk only; no baseline energy change.
counterfactual_or_caveat: Do not code proposal as implemented policy or treat the proposed numerical targets as observed outcomes.
causal_status: Not an implemented policy; no causal effect estimated
